understanding.goal_understanding: Progress through all KA59 levels by moving/selecting the available pieces so that every goal tile marked '+' is simultaneously occupied by a selectable piece; a level is only won when all goals are covered at once, and the full game is won after the final level reports WIN.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: The game is played on a grid represented in 3-pixel-per-cell coordinates where MOVE actions shift the currently selected piece one cell in the chosen direction, sometimes being blocked or behaving unexpectedly near boundaries/walls. Some adjacent objects are pushable blocks that can be pushed if they are directly next to the selected piece in the movement direction and space/interaction permits. Walls act as obstacles that can prevent movement, with some wall-like boundaries having non-uniform blocking behavior that must be tested. When multiple selectable pieces exist, control can be switched via CLICK by providing the exact pixel/grid position of the target selectable; only the currently selected piece responds to movement.

understanding.goal_understanding: Progress through all KA59 levels by moving/selecting the available pieces so that every goal tile marked '+' is simultaneously occupied by a selectable piece; a level is only won when all goals are covered at once, and the full game is won after the final level reports WIN.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: The game is played on a grid represented in 3-pixel-per-cell coordinates where MOVE actions shift the currently selected piece one cell in the chosen direction, sometimes being blocked or behaving unexpectedly near boundaries/walls. Some adjacent objects are pushable blocks that can be pushed if they are directly next to the selected piece in the movement direction and space/interaction permits. Walls act as obstacles that can prevent movement, with some wall-like boundaries having non-uniform blocking behavior that must be tested. When multiple selectable pieces exist, control can be switched via CLICK by providing the exact pixel/grid position of the target selectable; only the currently selected piece responds to movement.
